You are the Extractor agent in a newsroom verification pipeline. You read one SEC filing
document and record what the employer itself says about job cuts and AI. You record claims only.
You never infer causation, never paraphrase quotes and never use a reporter's or analyst's framing.

Attribution labels (they describe what the EMPLOYER SAYS, never what is true):
- explicit: the employer's own words say AI, automation or machine learning is a reason for THESE job cuts
  (e.g. "we are reducing roles as AI now handles this work").
- partial: the employer mentions AI/automation in the same announcement as the cuts (strategy, reinvestment,
  "shifting resources to AI") but does not say AI caused the cuts.
- none: the employer announces cuts and does not connect them to AI or automation.

Return ONE JSON object with exactly these keys:
{
  "is_workforce_reduction": true | false,      // does the document announce job cuts / layoffs / a reduction in force?
  "company": string,                          // the employer's name as written in the document
  "event_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | null,          // date of the announcement or of the cuts, if stated
  "jobs_cut": integer | null,                 // number of positions cut, ONLY if the document states a number
  "jobs_cut_text": string | null,             // the exact words stating the number or percentage, copied verbatim
  "cut_quote": string | null,                 // the one sentence, copied VERBATIM, in which the document announces or
                                              // reports the job cuts; null when is_workforce_reduction is false
  "ai_attribution": "explicit" | "partial" | "none",
  "ai_quote": string | null,                  // 1-2 sentences copied VERBATIM (character for character) in which the
                                              // employer connects the cuts to AI/automation; null when attribution is none
  "notes": string                             // one short sentence on anything ambiguous
}
is_workforce_reduction is true ONLY when the document itself announces or reports job cuts. Mentions inside
forward-looking-statement disclaimers, risk-factor lists or legal boilerplate (e.g. "the effectiveness of our
restructuring and workforce reduction program", "artificial intelligence laws") do NOT count, and an AI quote must never
come from that boilerplate.
Copy quotes exactly as they appear, including punctuation. If the document states a percentage but no headcount,
set jobs_cut to null and put the percentage wording in jobs_cut_text. Output JSON only.

ASX Announcement | 23 October 2026
X2M Signs Agreement for 10MW AI-Enabled Data Centre
A high-density GPU data centre in regional Queensland with power and
government approvals secured, shortening the commercialisation timeline
• 10MW Queensland site secured: X2M has signed an agreement with a Queensland developer (the
“Developer”) for a 10MW AI-enabled data centre site with development approval, which X2M
intends to deliver and manage under its Managed Delivery service.
• Binding exclusivity: X2M has been granted binding exclusivity over the data centre site and its
power capacity for 60 days, with commercial terms to be agreed and binding long-form agreements
targeted within 90 days.
• Queensland site with energy and approvals in place: The site has an existing 2.5MW grid
connection and local government development approval for a data centre, with the Developer to
build its own behind-the-meter generation to supply an additional 7.5MW under a power purchase
agreement. This is expected to result in earlier project completion and revenue recognition.
• $250m estimated project cost: The 10MW data centre intended for the location will have a project
cost of $250 million and is planned to be delivered through X2M’s compute and GPU partnerships
and it is currently expected that X2M will manage the elements of the full project cost and earn a
margin on this project, plus X2M is expected to earn recurring revenue from AI-enabled
management of the facility and a potential token revenue share.
• 20MW across two agreements: Together with its first binding agreement (ASX: 27 August 2026),
X2M now has 20MW of data centre capacity under agreement, with an aggregate estimated project
cost of more than $500m, along with its 200MW+ pipeline.
• More compute from less power: X2M’s AI-enabled platform is expected to produce the same
compute from fewer electricity megawatts, addressing one of the sector’s central constraints as
available grid capacity limits the pace of data centre build-out.
• Risk reduced by design: X2M is targeting data centres on sites in low-population-density regional
areas of Queensland and the Northern Territory, where there is greater access to land and power,
and capacity can be built up as grid energy is secured or a behind-the-meter micro grid is built.
X2M Connect Limited (ASX: X2M) (“X2M” or “the Company”) advises that it has signed an agreement with a
Queensland developer (the “Developer”) for a 10MW AI-enabled data centre site with development
approval and with power to be generated on the site for 10 years. Under the Agreement, X2M has been
granted binding exclusivity over the data centre site and its power capacity for 60 days, with commercial
terms to be agreed and binding long-form agreements targeted within 90 days.
The agreement follows X2M’s first binding data centre agreement (ASX: 27 August 2026) and sits alongside a
series of non-binding agreements that take X2M’s prospective pipeline above 200MW.
X2M intends to provide its Managed Delivery service across the design, engineering, supply, installation and
commissioning of the facility, followed by ongoing AI-enabled platform services and management for the life
of the asset.

Grid Connection and Government Approvals in Place
The site has an existing 2.5MW grid connection, together with development approval for the data centre.
The data centre will be delivered in stages with the initial stage utilising the existing grid capacity, with faster
commercialisation expected given the approvals and power are already in place.
The Developer intends to build behind-the-meter renewable generation to supply the balance of the energy
under a power purchase agreement, supporting the final 7.5MW and taking the facility to the full 10MW.
This power is expected to be available to the site by the end of the 2028 calendar year.
X2M’s platform is intended to manage energy, cooling and environmental systems across both grid-supplied
and behind-the-meter supply.
De-risked by Targeting Modular Regional Data Centres with Land, Power and Scalability
X2M is targeting data centre facilities in low-density population regions of Queensland and the Northern
Territory, rather than large metropolitan campuses, placing less demand on the grid and requiring a smaller
capital commitment.
As part of X2M’s due diligence process, power, land and government approval are assessed at every site
before a binding agreement is signed.
X2M’s AI-enabled platform is also designed to reduce the energy required to deliver a given level of
compute. With energy the binding constraint on data centre growth, more compute from every approved
megawatt is a key reason customers partner with X2M.
X2M also looks for developers and customers with the capability to build their own behind-the-meter micro
grid, giving the facility energy security independent of the grid and allowing the site to be scaled up beyond
its approved grid capacity.
X2M Continues to Convert 200MW+ Pipeline into Data Centre Capacity Under Agreement
Together with its 10MW first binding agreement, X2M now has 20MW of data centre capacity under
agreement with an aggregate estimated project cost of more than $500m. Design work under that
agreement (ASX: 27 August 2026) has confirmed its initial capacity of 10MW.
The agreement shows X2M is continuing to convert its prospective pipeline into agreements, with that
pipeline remaining above 200MW and the majority of sites in Queensland.
X2M CEO Mohan Jesudason said: “X2M is building two strong businesses in smart city digitisation and data
centre development. This agreement gives X2M 20MW of data centre capacity across two projects.
Queensland is where the majority of our pipeline sits, and this site already has energy and local government
approval in place, with planned behind-the-meter generation to carry it to the full 10MW. This agreement
will bring both our Managed Delivery and Platform Services products to this Queensland site. Our focus is
now on delivery and on converting the balance of our pipeline, including the partnership agreements already
announced.”
Ends
The Board of X2M has approved this announcement.
